name: Temporary residence permit for studies (zezwolenie na pobyt czasowy w celu kształcenia się na studiach)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires admission to full-time studies (or a preparatory course for higher education, or a PhD programme) at a Polish institution.
requirements.fix_path: Secure an admission letter from an accredited Polish university or preparatory programme.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants must show a stable and regular source of funds for the duration of study, referenced to the social-assistance income threshold for a single person (currently just above PLN 1,010/month net; some voivodeship offices apply the lower per-person-in-household figure of PLN 823/month depending on circumstances).
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements, a scholarship confirmation, or a sponsorship declaration from a person obliged to support the applicant.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants need health insurance (NFZ or private) covering the stay in Poland.
requirements.fix_path: Enrol in the Polish national health fund (NFZ) as a student or purchase qualifying private travel/health insurance.

evidence_required.document: Admission/enrolment confirmation from the Polish institution
Proof of tuition payment where applicable

outcome.duration_length: up to 15 months for the first permit (or up to program length for programs under 1 year); renewed for subsequent years of study

sources.title: Office for Foreigners (gov.pl/udsc-en) -- residence permits for study and post-graduation
Migrant.info.pl (IOM / Polish Ministry of Interior co-funded portal) -- Temporary residence permit for studies, corroborating admission and funds conditions

notes: Full work rights during studies is a genuinely favourable feature relative to several other countries in this dataset (e.g. Germany's 120-full/240-half-day cap for Blue Card-track non-EU students) -- Poland places no statutory cap on hours worked by full-time students holding this permit, since 2018 amendments exempted students from the labour-market test and hours restriction entirely. A closely related route not separately encoded here: graduates of Polish higher education institutions can obtain a one-time 9-month 'graduate' temporary residence permit (permit for temporary residence -- graduate) exempting them from the labour-market test while job-hunting, confirmed via gov.pl/udsc-en. This functions similarly to Germany's job-seeker permit or the Netherlands' Zoekjaar but is narrower (Polish-graduates only, 9 months, one-time) -- flagged as a candidate for a future separate route file rather than folded in here, to keep this file's requirement grammar clean around enrolled status specifically.
